executive_assessment.text: Basseterre and named low-lying settlements face water and coastal risks; informal-worker integration limits access to resilience planning and recovery.
Dieppe Bay, Sandy Point/Pump Bay and Newcastle Bay provide specific livelihood and infrastructure examples from participatory assessments, not representative island-wide measurements.
Reported warning/planning outputs and 2026 water projects are potential capacities. Operational status, prospective yields and verified impacts must remain distinct.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-11 reports: Most urban settlements are on low-lying coastal plains; TNC names Basseterre, Sandy Point, Charlestown and Newcastle.
Source dated 2024-11 reports: Nevis data and downscaled-information gaps limit community-scale planning; Sandy Point and school warning systems exist, but health has none.

Source dated 2022-11 reports: Basseterre, home to about 27% of the population, scores medium-high on fisheries, coastal ecosystems, water and economic risks; heat and hurricanes are prominent indicators.

Source dated 2022-11 reports: The report states 51% of renewable freshwater was withdrawn, 31 wells supplied 70% of potable water, and 2017 drought brought severe rationing; Basseterre Valley holds the main aquifer.

Source dated 2022-11 reports: Basseterre interviews identify difficulty reaching informal workers with policy; their limited institutional integration impedes inclusion in resilience planning and recovery.

Source dated 2022 reports: Dieppe Bay participants described homes, buildings, landing facilities and roads as exposed on a windward coast with little setback; erosion affects the settlement and coastal protection.
Source dated 2022 reports: Hurricane Irma destroyed the Capisterre cooperative in 2017; it remained unrepaired at the 2020 assessment, leaving fishers without storage or processing space.
Source dated 2022 reports: Sandy Point participants linked Pump Bay erosion and past storms that damaged the cooperative and pier with difficulty hauling and securing fishing boats.

Source dated 2022 reports: Newcastle Bay fishers reported erosion and storm damage to the landing site and pier; the Foundation organized participation and UNDP/GEF grants supported lockers, but further facilities were requested.

The June 2026 ministry update reports that Basseterre desalination began service in February, restoring round-the-clock supply for about 20,000 customers. The higher-elevation Saint Peters pipeline and pump were installed but still being tested at publication; operation there is not confirmed.
Source dated 2026-06-18 reports: The ministry projects ten candidate wells could yield up to four million gallons daily and meet demand through 2040; drilling at Saddlers began in January 2026.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 12 of 12 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

No verified country-specific source-stated climate-change-to-organized-conflict or organized-conflict-to-adaptation-constraint pathway was located. The TNC's storm-displacement/GBV pathway is qualitative and projected.
The 2023 Voluntary National Review PDF surfaced in indexed search, but direct open returned HTTP 403; indexed text was not used as evidence.
Participatory coastal findings focus on three selected fishing communities and small workshop samples; these do not support representative island-wide prevalence estimates.
Local information was strongest for Basseterre and selected coastal fishing communities; evidence on climate vulnerability and adaptation in other parishes is thinner.

The TNC lists a qualitative stronger-storm/displacement/sexual-violence risk but gives no projection period for that row. It is retained in the research audit and excluded from the runtime projection rather than inventing a medium-term horizon.
No complete supported climate-to-organized-violence or reverse-FCV pathway was verified. Informal-worker exclusion and storm protection risks are not evidence of armed conflict.
Selected fishing-community observations are small purposive samples from around 2020, not island-wide prevalence or current infrastructure status.
The June 2026 ministry account is official self-report: Basseterre service is reported, Saint Peters equipment was still under testing, and candidate-well yields are prospective.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
